proof.criterion: The note's cause is the measured one, and a reader following it puts large writes on the issue volume rather than anywhere the container filesystem holds.
proof.surface: A live Legion role container — this issue's own implementer container in its Agent Sandbox issue pod on the production cluster, the exact surface the note is about.
proof.command: cat /proc/mounts; stat -c '%n dev=%d' /tmp /home/legion /home/legion/.cache /home/legion/.config /legion /var/run/legion/state /var/run/legion/private /var/run/legion/gh /home/legion/.local/state; then, around each 200 MiB write, df -k --output=used / with dd if=/dev/zero of=<path>/probe bs=1M count=200 for <path> in /tmp, /home/legion/.cache, /legion and /home/legion/.config
proof.observed: /proc/mounts carries no /tmp line. stat gives device 114 for /tmp, /home/legion, /home/legion/.cache and /home/legion/.local/state alike; 118 for /legion; 56 for /home/legion/.config; 128 for /var/run/legion/state; 130 for /var/run/legion/private; 124 for /var/run/legion/gh. df -k --output=used / reads 14392 KiB at rest, 219192 KiB with the 200 MiB file under /tmp, 14392 KiB again once it is removed, and 219192 KiB with the same file under /home/legion/.cache. So /tmp and the home directory are one charged container filesystem, which is what the note now says and the opposite of the cluster read's one wrong sentence.
proof.negativeControl: The same 200 MiB written under /home/legion/.config (device 56, an in-memory volume) left / at 14392 KiB and grew that volume to 204808 KiB, and the write under /legion left / at 14392 KiB while /legion grew to 839284 KiB. The method therefore distinguishes a memory-backed or volume-backed path from a charged one and would have shown /tmp as uncharged had it been memory-backed. A second control on the instrument: du -sx / reported no change for any of these writes (gVisor's overlay reports 0 blocks for such a file), which is why the note cites df on / rather than du.

du is the wrong instrument on this runtime. A 200 MiB file under /tmp shows 0 blocks to `du` on the pod's gVisor overlay, so `du -sx /` reports no change at all; only `df -k --output=used /` sees the charge. A proof of this criterion written with `du` would have produced a false negative in both directions.

`bunx biome check .` is not a usable local check in a role container with no node_modules: bunx resolves an unrelated registry package named `biome` (version 0.3.3) and exits 0 having checked nothing. Biome 2.4.11 has no markdown rules anyway, so the authoritative check for this diff is CI's lint job, which is what the proof cites. `bun install` was deliberately not run — its node_modules would be a large write onto exactly the charged filesystem this note is about.
The golden pod JSON gives each role container four /var/run/legion/* mounts (launcher, private, state, gh), not the three an earlier reading reported; the note says four.
